symbols.name: matrix entry
symbols.meaning: The entry of the matrix $A$ in row $i$ and column $j$, an element of $F$.
symbols.quote: The entry of $A$ in row $i$ and column $j$ is written $A_{ij}$, an element of $F$, for $i,j$ from $1$ to $m$.

symbols.name: transpose
symbols.meaning: The matrix obtained from $A$ by exchanging rows and columns, whose entry in row $i$ and column $j$ is $A_{ji}$.
symbols.quote: The *transpose* $A^{\top}$ is the $m\times m$ matrix whose entry in row $i$ and column $j$ is $A_{ji}$, so its rows are the columns of $A$.

symbols.name: three-element subset
symbols.meaning: A three-element subset of a finite set, one of the two triples compared for neighbourhood.
symbols.quote: Let $S$ and $T$ be three-element subsets of a finite set.

symbols.name: three-element subset
symbols.meaning: A three-element subset of a finite set, the second triple compared with $S$.
symbols.quote: Let $S$ and $T$ be three-element subsets of a finite set.

relations.quote: A symmetric matrix is a special case of the matrices in [Linear algebra basics](linear-algebra-basics.md): a square matrix equal to its own transpose.
